authoredFrom: SOL-18 — per-symbol complexity and `ownerKind`. Authored 2026-09-30 from the analyzer's measured output. Before SOL-18 every Solidity symbol reported complexity 1: `pool-worker.ts` defaults to `s.complexity || s.metadata?.complexity || 1` and the analyzer set neither, so the field was populated across the whole corpus with a constant that reads as a measurement. Over 389 files it now reaches 25, with 690 symbols above 1.
note: Complexity is attributed through the FRAME stack as the walk proceeds — one increment per branch node, no second traversal per declaration, which is the cost the TypeScript lane measured and removed. The bug this fixture exists to pin was silent: `declareSymbol` CALLED `pushSymbol` and discarded the result, so every frame carried `sym: null`, the exit branch had nothing to write to, and `symbolsWithComplexity` was 0 — a feature that measured nothing while still reporting the pool-worker's default of 1. `straight` is the shape that makes a measured 1 distinguishable from a defaulted 1. `loopAndTernary` pins the counting rule: `else` is PART of `if_statement` in this grammar, so an if/else pair is ONE branch, and a rule counting the two keywords separately would report 4 here. `oneBranch` shows a modifier body counting its own branches. `ownerKind` is pinned on the INTERFACE and LIBRARY members as well as the contract's, because a member of a library reporting `contract` would be a plausible-looking wrong answer. `fromLibrary` was pinned as `contract` when this fixture was first written — a bug in SOL-18 itself: `declareSymbol` maps BOTH `contract_declaration` and `library_declaration` to `SymbolKind.Class`, so deriving ownerKind from the Kind reported every library member as a contract member. Found by reading `contracts/utils/Strings.sol` back, not by any gate, and it is the second time in two commits that a `SymbolKind` collapse has cost a real distinction: the first was `return_parameter` vs `parameter`.

expectSymbols.name: i
expectSymbols.comment: A local variable's owner is the FUNCTION, not a type, so `ownerKind` must be ABSENT. `forbidSymbols` was the wrong instrument for this — it asserts the symbol does not exist at all, and `i` exists; the right home is an `expectSymbols` row with a null value, which reads as 'this field must be absent or null'. A rule that fell back to the enclosing declaration would report 'contract' here.
